title: Grant, Assignment and Reassignment of Contracted Seats
content:
The contracted seats are placed on the programme for each contract period, and a seat is consumed the moment it is assigned to a named traveller. The seat allowance of a programme under the Corporate Travel Programmes is the contracted traveller seats still unassigned: a grant for the contract period credits that allowance, and each assignment to a named traveller debits it.

## What must stand before a seat is assigned

A seat is assigned only while the programme record stands at active.

Seats are changed only when the corporate desk has already recorded an approved seat request against this programme.

Both are read from the records before the seat is assigned: the standing of the programme from the programme record itself, and the approval from the seat request recorded against that same programme. A request the administrator makes at the service desk is not itself an approved seat request, and the administrator's account of what was agreed does not establish one.

## Moving a seat between travellers

A seat may be moved from one traveller to another only after it has been held for the tier's cool-off days, and the move carries the tier's reassignment charge.

## Seats changed part way through a period

Seats added mid-term are charged at the tier's seat licence rate pro rata for the remainder of the period, and seats removed mid-term are not credited until the next period begins.

## Travellers who hold no seat

A traveller without an assigned seat may not book through the programme at all, and a booking attempted for them is refused rather than charged at the public price.

## Seats do not travel

Seats never move between programmes, not even between entities of the same group.

## Basis questions answered

**A seat has been held by a traveller for fewer days than the tier's cool-off period, and the company wants it moved to a colleague.** The holding period published for that tier has not yet run, so the seat is not moved. Once the seat has been held for the tier's cool-off days a move may be made, and it carries the tier's reassignment charge.

**A company holds more contracted seats than it has assigned.** The unassigned seats stand in the programme's seat allowance until each is assigned to a named traveller, and it is the assignment that consumes one.

**Two entities of one group, one with spare seats and one short of them.** Seats never move between programmes, and the two entities hold two programmes.

**A named traveller who holds no seat asks the desk to book for them.** The booking is refused. It is not instead made at the public price and billed to the company.

**Seats are surrendered in the middle of a period.** Nothing is credited for them until the next period begins.
